title: Evaluation Metrics
subtitle: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, and MSE

content.text: Accuracy alone is misleading on imbalanced datasets. Use precision, recall, and F1 for classification; RMSE or MAE for regression.

content.code:
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score,
    f1_score, roc_auc_score, confusion_matrix
)

acc = accuracy_score(y_test, preds)
prec = precision_score(y_test, preds)
rec = recall_score(y_test, preds)
f1 = f1_score(y_test, preds)
auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, probs)

print(f"Accuracy: {acc:.3f}  Precision: {prec:.3f}")
print(f"Recall:   {rec:.3f}  F1: {f1:.3f}  AUC: {auc:.3f}")
print(confusion_matrix(y_test, preds))

questions.question: In a cancer screening model, which is more important?
questions.explanation: Missing a cancer case (false negative) is more dangerous than a false alarm, so recall matters more.

faq.a: The Area Under the ROC Curve measures discrimination ability across all thresholds. 1.0 is perfect; 0.5 is random.
